summary: This is a fragment of a Maven build file (pom.xml) that adds the Mockito library to the project so tests can create fake stand-ins for real objects, such as a TemperatureSensor that does not exist yet.

lines.text: Maven builds keep every outside library the project needs inside this one block, so adding a tool means declaring it here rather than downloading a file by hand.
An XML comment marking where the JUnit 5 entry already sits; Mockito is added alongside JUnit, not instead of it, since Mockito supplies the fakes while JUnit still runs the tests.
The groupId and artifactId together name the exact library Maven should fetch, the way a first and last name identify one person; mockito-core is the mocking engine itself.
Pinning an exact version keeps the build reproducible, so the code that passes today does not break tomorrow when a newer Mockito is released.
The test scope makes Mockito available to test code only, keeping it out of the shipped application; mocking is a testing technique and production code should never depend on it.
